findings.quote: 1. Meiosis divides the nucleus into four haploid nuclei.
findings.problem: This step is stated without a limit inside the example on oogenesis, and it is false for that case. In human oogenesis the first polar body may or may not go through meiosis II, so one germ cell gives one egg and one to three polar bodies. That is three or four haploid nuclei, not always four. The lesson itself says elsewhere that 'A typical meiosis gives four haploid cells. There are developmental exceptions.', but this step drops the limit in exactly the exceptional case. The final answer (4 sperm, 1 egg) is right.
findings.source: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 27.2: the first polar body 'may or may not complete meiosis and produce second polar bodies'; Figure 27.11 caption: 'one to three polar bodies'. Reader rules, Added after the Sol audit (test general statements against a known exception).

findings.quote: In most animals, a body cell holds chromosomes in pairs. Each pair is a **homologous pair**.
findings.problem: Together with the next paragraph ('Homologs carry the same genes in the same order.') this says that every chromosome pair in a body cell carries the same genes in the same order. The X and Y pair of human males (and of other XY animals) is the standard exception: X and Y are not completely homologous and share only a small region. Example #3 then applies the rule to all humans ('$46$ chromosomes, or $23$ homologous pairs'). A student taught this rule with no exception could conclude that X and Y carry the same genes, which conflicts with sex-linked inheritance.
findings.source: OpenStax Biology 2e, 11.1: 'the X and Y sex chromosomes are not completely homologous'; 'a small region of homology that allows the X and Y chromosomes to pair up during prophase I'. Reader rules, Added after the Sol audit.

findings.quote: A **eukaryotic cell** is a cell with a nucleus. The nucleus holds the cell's DNA. DNA is packaged into **chromosomes**, and each chromosome carries many **genes**.
findings.problem: This paragraph has five sentences, over the limit of one to three short sentences. The paragraphs starting 'In animals, meiosis happens in **germ cells**' (five sentences) and 'A typical meiosis gives four haploid cells.' (four sentences) also go over.
findings.source: Content checklist L22a; LSG Formatting rules (paragraphs of 1 to 3 short sentences).
